prompt:
Create a transparent-background pixel-art atlas with exactly THREE equal square cells side-by-side labeled by order FRONT, TOP, REAR for the same Iron Tracks rail buffer stop in the canonical source. Attached contact labels the native source and accepted RIGHT/LEFT/BOTTOM. Use source for rail identity/material; accepted side views for the triangular timber/steel support geometry and accepted underside for ground footprint. Camera directions are strict orthographic principal views, no isometric/perspective.

FRONT and REAR look horizontally along the track axis toward opposite ends. Show thin end elevation: low gravel/railbed edge at ground, two compact steel feet/support ends, the horizontal red buffer beam spanning track width, and its source gray bolted clamps. Do not show an overhead rail-bed plane or full track-length triangle.

TOP looks straight down: the rail pair and short wooden sleepers remain narrow longitudinal strips; the red buffer is only a thin transverse red bar at the end of the rails, with its two gray mounting blocks. The red bar must be seen edge-on from above, not as a broad upright red face. Keep the native footprint and orientation. Preserve dark iron rails, brown sleepers, orange/brown ballast, red beam and steel braces. No invented signal lights, no stray detached objects. Center, transparent margin, no labels, clipping, shadow or guide marks; crisp pixel art.
